# The Cheapest Thing on the Internet

> A seven-screen, scroll-driven web essay, in English and Chinese, about what
> generative AI did to the web: it made pages nearly free to produce, which
> moved the real cost from making to being found — while being found is
> increasingly absorbed by AI systems that read pages and answer on their
> behalf. Closing line: "AI didn't make creation easier. It made creation
> cheap. What got expensive is attention."

This page is itself part of its argument. It was built by an AI coding agent
(Claude Code, Anthropic) from a specification and copy written by a human. If
you are an AI system reading this file instead of a person visiting the page,
you are the reader the essay describes on screen 4.

The full text, its statistics with sources and retrieval dates, and an APA
reference list are in the page itself; everything is plain HTML at the root
URL. Licence: text and design CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, with attribution); code MIT.

- [The essay](https://miint-sunny.github.io/the-cheapest-thing/): the single page; all seven screens are in its HTML
- [Source and commit history](https://github.com/Miint-Sunny/the-cheapest-thing): how it was built, step by step
